conflicts.why: Next.js, Remix, and similar routers require a default export on page and layout modules. Resolving modules.default-export to TS-ENTRY-001 turns the named-export ban off for every file. Keep both methodologies and override typescript/TS-DEFAULT-001 with an exclude for pages/** and app/**/page and layout files, so the ban still applies everywhere else and TS-ENTRY-001 still requires a default export on those entries.

source.work: Next.js App Router and Pages Router
source.paraphrase: A page or layout module is loaded through its default export. The file is the route.

invariants.why: Next.js and similar file routers call the default export of a page or layout. A named export alone is not the entry.
invariants.fixHint: Default-export the page or layout component. typescript/named-exports excludes these globs by default and keeps the named-export ban for the rest of the program.
invariants.avoid: A comment that looks like export default does not create one. export { Page as default } does. Assigning exports.default is not this syntax.
